Closest reproducible prior: [Sequential Rules](https://github.com/rn5l/session-rec/blob/master/algorithms/baselines/sr.py) counts directed transitions across bounded distances, supports inverse-distance decay, recency-weighted history aggregation, optional IDF, and per-source pruning. [PCTM](https://github.com/spotify-research/sequential-capacity-probes) combines smoothed multi-distance transition estimates with recency weighting and popularity adjustment; its official repository includes graph-only MC and Sequential Rules baselines and full-catalog ranking. These substantially anticipate the proposed estimator’s components, although I found no verified source specifying the exact combination of positive log-lift and separate edge/source support shrinkage.

Positive log-lift is PPMI when source and destination marginals use the same transition-event distribution. Rare-event inflation is established: [Damani (2013)](https://aclanthology.org/W13-3503/) incorporates significant co-occurrence into PMI. A reproducible proposed variant—not a formula attributed to these papers—is W_ij = [log(((c_ij+αp_j)/(c_i+α))/p_j)]₊ × c_ij/(c_ij+β) × c_i/(c_i+γ), followed by recency-weighted prefix summation. Specify destination prior p_j, transition window, distance weights, repeated-item handling, and support-count definitions. Smoothing and the two shrinkage factors need separate ablations.

Implementation assessment: straightforward with sparse rows; store observed positive edges, optionally retain top-K destinations/source, and use sorted-row binary search or hashing for candidate lookup. For full-catalog residuals, scatter-add weighted history rows into catalog score buffers, then combine with chunked neural scores; missing edges contribute zero. This is an engineering recommendation. Report target-edge coverage before/after pruning, zero-residual frequency, support/degree strata, memory, and latency per category. Compare graph-only, SASRec-only, and combined scores under the pinned evaluator. [Han et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07125) further motivates local-transition diagnostics. Assessment: modest methodological novelty; high implementation feasibility, with gains and scalability requiring measurement.
